speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: asked the Minister for Education (Schools) (a) what is the number of students who suffer from depression and other mental conditions over the last five years; (b) what are the main causes for such cases; and (c) what resources are channelled towards identifying and watching out for the at-risk students.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: First, how are teachers trained to identify at-risk children?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Second, for every child, how do the schools then work with their family, Family Service Centres and mental health clinics to help them?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Third, for the children who are identified in Primary school and moving on to Secondary school, is there a process for the schools to pass information to the next education institution?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is not something that is an aside; it is something central to how teachers are trained to react to and to interact with the behaviour of students.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, as part of that training, coming out of that, abnormalities of behaviour, abnormalities of adjustments, abnormalities of coping are very much part of what would be considered the core of teacher training.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are instances where they prefer for this information not to be shared and to work with community partners or healthcare partners and not actually discuss this with the teacher.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is hard to say whether this is ideal or optimal, because it is a very wide field, and there will be circumstances where it is appropriate for the family, for the child to make that decision and keep the matter private.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But, in general, it would be better if the teachers could be involved in this process.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But I do not think we want to be prescriptive about this process.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If we talk in general terms, we do want some opportunity for privacy, for some opportunity of parental consent and for the child to have some control over the issue, especially if it is an issue that is resolved and is no longer causing any problem or affecting the child.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: On the other hand, for the same circumstance, you can make an argument that the educators in the Secondary school need to know on the basis of the child's risk of something happening.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But not to be prescriptive again, is whether to perhaps remove entirely the family and the child's ability to have some input into that process of privacy.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We take it and, in general, we would hope that the education service could play a role in helping these children.
